title: Guaranteed Noisy CP Tensor Recovery via Riemannian Optimization on the Segre Manifold
claim: Our geometry-aware methods converge faster and to lower error than baselines across noise levels and correlation settings, reaching the statistical floor.
layout: 4x4 grid of line plots, rows by noise level, columns by correlation
description: A 4x4 grid of small-multiple line plots showing log10 relative error (RMSE) against iteration, 0 to 20, with one shared legend on top. Rows are noise settings: noiseless, SNR 30, SNR 10 and SNR 3. Columns are predictor correlation rho = 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75. Each panel has a grey title strip. Four methods are drawn with distinct colors and markers: CP-ALS (green squares), RRR (dark purple triangles), RGD (salmon circles) and RGN (cyan triangles). In the noiseless row, RGN drops steeply to the 1e-15 floor, CP-ALS follows, and RGD descends linearly. RRR stalls near -1.5. In noisy rows, all methods except RRR quickly plateau at the same noise floor. The y-axis label is shared on the left and the x-axis label, Iteration, is shared at the bottom.
caption: Convergence for CP tensor-on-tensor regression with rank r = 3. Each curve is the root mean square, over 20 replications, of the relative Frobenius error. RRR uses a random start, and errors above 1 are omitted. Errors below 10−15 are drawn at 10−15. Point symbols are drawn at staggered iterations so that coinciding curves remain distinguishable.
abstract: Recovering a low-CP-rank tensor from noisy linear measurements is a central challenge in high-dimensional data analysis, with applications spanning tensor PCA, scalar-on-tensor regression, tensor-on-tensor regression, and beyond. We exploit the intrinsic geometry of rank-one tensors by casting the recovery task as an optimization problem over the Segre manifold, the smooth Riemannian manifold of rank-one tensors. This geometric viewpoint yields two powerful algorithms: Riemannian Gradient Descent (RGD) and Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN), each of which preserves feasibility at every iteration. Under mild noise assumptions, we prove that RGD converges at a local linear rate, while RGN exhibits an initial local quadratic phase followed by linear refinement to the statistical error. Extensive synthetic experiments validate these convergence guarantees and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.
